title: Push-Payment Denial of Service
summary: A distributor pushes ETH to every registered participant in a loop and requires each send to succeed. A single participant whose receive() reverts makes the whole loop revert, so nobody can be paid and the funds are frozen.
web2Analog: A batch job that aborts the entire run on the first failed item — one poisoned record blocks processing for everyone (no isolation / no dead-letter handling).

identify.question: Why can one participant freeze everyone's funds?
options: distribute() pushes to each participant and reverts the whole loop if any single send fails
share is computed with integer division
the contract has a receive() function
identify.explanation: distribute() does `require(ok)` on every push inside the loop. A participant whose receive() reverts makes that send fail, reverting the entire transaction — so no one is ever paid and the balance is stuck.

hints: distribute() sends to every participant in one transaction and insists each send succeeds.
What happens to the whole loop if just one recipient's receive() reverts?
Register a contract whose receive() reverts, then distribute() can never complete.
The robust fix is the pull-payment pattern (let each user withdraw their own share); a minimal fix stops one failed send from reverting the others.
